meta.title: Documents | Welcome to Brazil
meta.desc: How to get a CPF, RNM, Digital Work Card, CadÚnico and SUS card in São Paulo, and how to apply for refugee status.

docs.title: Documents
docs.lead: Start with the CPF and the registration with the Federal Police. With them, it is easier to get the other documents.

cpf.title: CPF
cpf.what: The CPF is your taxpayer number with the Receita Federal (Brazil's tax agency). You need it to work, open a bank account and use many services.

where.1: Fill in the Receita Federal online form for foreigners. You will get a protocol number.
where.2: Take the protocol and your documents to a Receita Federal office. The service is free there.
where.3: You can also go to a Correios (post office), Banco do Brasil or Caixa branch, or to a registry office (cartório). These places charge a fee of R$ 7.00.

bring.1: Photo ID, such as a passport or CRNM.
bring.2: Birth or marriage certificate, if your ID does not show your place and date of birth and your parents' names.
bring.3: The protocol number, if you filled in the online form.

rnm.title: RNM and CRNM
rnm.what: The RNM (National Migration Registration) is your registration number with the Federal Police. The CRNM is the card with this number. It is your ID document in Brazil.

who.1: If you entered with a temporary visa: register within 90 days of arrival.
who.2: If you received a residence permit: register within 30 days of its publication in the Diário Oficial da União (official gazette).
who.3: Recognized refugees, asylees and stateless persons.

rnm.late: If you miss the deadline, you may be fined.

how.1: Fill in the Federal Police online form and pay the fee (GRU payment slip).
how.3: Go to the Federal Police office for the area where you live, on your appointment day.
how.4: Pick up your card at the Federal Police. It usually takes about 30 working days.

bring.1: The list of documents depends on your case. Check the official page before you go.
bring.2: Proof of payment of the fee.

cost.1: Card fee: R$ 204.77. Booking the appointment is free.
cost.2: The Migration Law provides for fee exemption for vulnerable people or people who cannot afford to pay. Ask for guidance at CRAI or at the Federal Public Defender's Office (DPU).

refuge.title: Applying for refugee status
refuge.what: If you left your country because of persecution or serious human rights violations, you can apply for refugee status in Brazil. Applying is free.

how.1: Create an account on SisCONARE, the Ministry of Justice system, using your own email. You can fill in the form in Portuguese, Spanish, English or French.
how.2: At the end, you will get a control number.
how.3: Go to the Federal Police with this number, a 3x4 photo and any documents you have. Each family member must go.
how.4: The Federal Police will give you the Refugee Protocol. It works as your ID document in Brazil. Renew the protocol every year while your application is being reviewed.
how.5: Log in to SisCONARE at least once a month to see notices, such as the date of your interview.

refuge.note: Not having documents does not stop you from applying. With the protocol, you can get a CPF and a work card.

ctps.title: Digital Work Card (Carteira de Trabalho Digital)
ctps.what: It is the record of your jobs, on your phone. The card number is your CPF. With a formal job registered on the card, you have access to labor rights.

how.2: Create a gov.br account (bronze, silver or gold level).
how.3: Download the Carteira de Trabalho Digital app (Android or iPhone) or use the Ministry of Labor website. The card is issued right away.

ctps.help: Questions: call 158, the Ministry of Labor and Employment helpline.

cad.title: CadÚnico
cad.what: The Cadastro Único is the government register for low-income families. It gives access to social programs, such as Bolsa Família and the Social Electricity Tariff.

who.1: Families with an income of up to half the minimum wage per person.
who.2: In the city of São Paulo, a municipal law guarantees immigrants access to public services, whatever their migration status.

where.1: At the CRAS (Social Assistance Reference Center) near your home.
where.2: In São Paulo, book in advance by calling 156 or on the City Hall (Prefeitura) website.
where.3: The interview takes about 1 hour. It is free.

bring.1: From the person responsible for the family: CPF, photo ID and proof of address (or a declaration of residence).
bring.2: From the other family members: one document for each person.

cad.verify: The official list does not mention foreign documents. Check at the CRAS or by calling 121 which documents are accepted.
cad.linkSp: CadÚnico at São Paulo City Hall

sus.title: SUS card
sus.what: It is the card of the Unified Health System (SUS). The SUS is public and free. It serves everyone, of any nationality or migration status.

where.1: At the UBS (Basic Health Unit) closest to your home.
where.2: To find your UBS, use the City Hall's Busca Saúde and choose “Moro neste endereço” (I live at this address).
where.3: The CPF is also used as an ID number in the SUS.

bring.1: Photo ID, such as a passport, CRNM or Refugee Protocol.
bring.3: Under City Hall rules, the UBS should not require proof of address to register you.

sus.verify: We did not find an official list of documents for foreigners. Check at the UBS.

meta.title: Work | Welcome to Brazil
meta.desc: Labor rights of migrants and refugees, Digital Work Card, CV, courses and where to look for jobs in São Paulo.

work.title: Work
work.lead: In Brazil, migrants and refugees have the same labor rights as Brazilians.

rights.1: With a formal job registered on your work card, you are entitled to the minimum wage, paid vacation, a 13th salary, FGTS and a weekly day off.
rights.2: The employer pays for the pre-employment medical exams.
rights.3: No one can keep your documents.
rights.4: No one can force you to work to pay off a debt.
rights.5: Discrimination based on nationality or migration status is prohibited.
rights.6: Even if your documents are not up to date, if you work you have labor rights.
rights.title: Your rights

report.1: Slave labor or human trafficking: call 100 or use the Ipê System online. You do not need to give your name.
report.2: Other questions about work: call 158, the Ministry of Labor and Employment helpline.
report.title: How to report

ctps.text: It is free and stays on your phone. To get it, you need a CPF and a gov.br account.
ctps.jobs: In the app, the “Vagas de emprego” (job vacancies) area shows Sine jobs that match your profile and address.
ctps.link: See how to get the work card

cv.1: Use only one page, in simple Portuguese.
cv.2: Include your name, phone number, email and the neighborhood where you live.
cv.3: Write the languages you speak and your level in each one.
cv.4: List your jobs, from the most recent to the oldest: position, company, country and period.
cv.5: Include education and courses. Studies done in another country also count.
cv.6: You do not need to include a photo, document numbers, religion or marital status.
cv.7: Ask someone to review it. Cate and the organizations on the “Where to get help” page can guide you.
cv.title: How to write a CV

courses.1: Portuguese: the City Hall's Portas Abertas program offers free classes for immigrants.
courses.2: Cate (Center for Work and Entrepreneurship Support), run by City Hall, offers jobs, guidance and training courses. The central unit serves immigrants, with bilingual staff.
courses.3: Some support organizations also offer courses. Ask them directly.
courses.title: Courses and training

jobs.1: Emprega Brasil portal (Sine), from the federal government. You log in with your gov.br account. It is free.
jobs.2: Carteira de Trabalho Digital app, in the “Vagas de emprego” area.
jobs.3: Cate, from São Paulo City Hall. Sometimes there are hiring events only for immigrants and refugees.
jobs.4: CRAI and support organizations, which share job openings and give guidance.
jobs.title: Where to look for jobs
jobs.warning: Be careful: do not trust job offers that ask for money to hire you or that want to keep your documents.

meta.title: Transport in SP | Welcome to Brazil
meta.desc: Bilhete Único, metro, train, bus, free fares and route apps in the city of São Paulo.

transport.title: Transport in São Paulo
transport.lead: Buses, metro and trains connect the city. With the Bilhete Único, you pay less when you change between them.

card.title: Bilhete Único
card.what: It is the card to pay for city buses, the metro and trains in São Paulo.

how.1: Register on the SPTrans service website and send a photo.
how.2: After approval, pick up the card at a service point, with photo ID. You can also ask for home delivery and pay for shipping.
how.3: Add credit at the top-up points listed by SPTrans.

card.one: Each person can have only one Bilhete Único.
card.anon: There is also a Bilhete Único without a name. To buy it, you need photo ID and a CPF.

integration.1: up to 4 different buses, paying a single fare;
integration.2: metro or train plus up to 3 buses, paying the integrated fare. The metro or train trip must be within the first 2 hours.
integration.title: Transfers: pay less when you change

card.price: Prices change. Check the current fare table on the SPTrans website.

rail.1: The metro and commuter trains connect many parts of the city and Greater São Paulo.
rail.2: Some lines are run by private companies, such as ViaQuatro and ViaMobilidade.
rail.3: You can pay with the Bilhete Único. Line maps are in the stations and on the official websites.
rail.title: Metro and train

bus.1: City buses are managed by SPTrans. To get on, tap your Bilhete Único on the card reader.
bus.2: Buses to other cities in the region are intercity buses (EMTU) and have other rules.
bus.title: Bus

sunday.1: On Sundays, city buses are free all day. This also applies on December 25, January 1 and January 25.
sunday.2: It does not apply to the metro, trains or intercity buses.
sunday.3: Even when it is free, tap your Bilhete Único on the card reader. If you have no card, ask the driver or the conductor for help.
sunday.title: Domingão Tarifa Zero (free Sundays)
sunday.verify: The program started in December 2023. Check on the SPTrans website whether it is still in effect.

free.1: People aged 60 or over ride city buses, the metro and trains for free. From 60 to 64, the free rides are loaded every month onto the regular Bilhete Único. From 65, there is the Special Bilhete Único for Older People.
free.2: Students: the Student Bilhete Único is requested by the school, which sends the data to SPTrans.
free.3: People with disabilities can request the Special Bilhete Único. Check the requirements with SPTrans.
free.4: Benefits for unemployed people and a social fare for low-income people: we did not confirm the current rules in an official source. Ask SPTrans, Metrô and CPTM.
free.title: Free fares and discounts

apps.1: Free map apps, such as Google Maps and Moovit, show which bus, metro or train to take.
apps.2: To use less mobile data, plan your route while on Wi-Fi and take a screenshot.
apps.3: The SPTrans, Metrô and CPTM websites also show lines and maps.
apps.title: Route apps

meta.title: Health, housing and education | Welcome to Brazil
meta.desc: Health clinics and SUS, shelters, school enrollment and free Portuguese courses for migrants and refugees in São Paulo.

life.title: Health, housing and education
life.lead: Health care and public school are rights of all people, of any nationality and migration status.

health.1: The SUS is public and free. It serves everyone, of any nationality or migration status.
health.2: The UBS (Basic Health Unit) is the first place to go: medical appointments, vaccines and referrals to specialists.
health.3: You can register at the UBS even before you register with the Federal Police.
health.4: To find the UBS for your address, use the City Hall's Busca Saúde.
health.5: AMA/UBS Pari has bilingual staff and signs in Spanish, English, French, Arabic and Chinese.
health.title: Health: UBS and SUS
health.emergency: Emergency: call 192 (SAMU) or go to an emergency room (pronto-socorro).
health.card: How to get the SUS card

shelter.1: City Hall has shelters, some only for immigrants.
shelter.2: To ask for a place, call 156 or go to the CREAS or CRAS in your area.
shelter.3: CRAI, the City Hall center for immigrants, can also guide you.
shelter.title: If you have nowhere to sleep

rent.1: Ask for a written contract and a receipt for every payment.
rent.2: Do not pay anything before you see the place.
rent.3: If you have questions about the contract, go to the Public Defender's Office (Defensoria Pública).
rent.title: Renting a place

school.1: Every child and teenager has the right to study in a public school, even without documents and whatever their migration status.
school.2: The school cannot refuse enrollment because of missing documents or a missing sworn translation. Documents can be handed in later.
school.3: Without school records, the school will assess the student to decide the right grade.
school.4: Go to the school closest to your home. If you have trouble, contact the Diretoria Regional de Educação (regional education office) or the Conselho Tutelar (child protection council).
school.title: School enrollment

pt.2: No documents needed. Migration status does not matter.
pt.3: Enrollment all year round, directly at the city schools that take part in the program.
pt.4: Basic, intermediate and advanced levels. Students with at least 75% attendance receive a certificate.
pt.title: Portuguese classes
pt.what: Portas Abertas is the City Hall's free Portuguese course for immigrants.

free.title: Services that are free
free.intro: No one can charge for these public services. If someone asks for money, it is a scam.
free.cpf: CPF done at the Receita Federal (at post offices, banks and registry offices the official fee is R$ 7.00)
free.sus: SUS card and care in the SUS
free.help: Services at CRAI and the Public Defender’s Office
free.crnm: The migration registration card (CRNM) has an official fee of R$ 204.77, paid only with a government payment slip (GRU). People who cannot pay can ask for an exemption.

scam.title: Signs of a scam
scam.1: They ask for money to get you a job, a place in a shelter or a document.
scam.2: They ask for a deposit or a Pix payment before you see the place to rent.
scam.3: They offer to exchange money on the street at a rate much better than the bank’s.
scam.4: They want to keep your passport or your documents.
scam.5: They pressure you to pay right away, with no time to think.
scam.r1: Problems with purchases, prices and services: Procon-SP.
scam.r2: Scam or crime: call 190 or file a police report at the Delegacia Eletrônica (online police station).
scam.r3: Slave labor or human trafficking: call 100.

meta.title: Where to get help | Welcome to Brazil
meta.desc: Emergency numbers and organizations that serve migrants and refugees in São Paulo, with address, phone and website.

help.title: Where to get help
help.lead: Public services and organizations that serve migrants and refugees. Services are free.
help.hours: We do not publish opening hours, because they change. Check before you go. Information marked “to be confirmed” has not yet been confirmed in an official source.

crai.name: CRAI Oriana Jara (São Paulo City Hall)
crai.desc: Reference center for immigrants, with services in several languages: migration status, social services, legal guidance and psychological support. The Federal Public Defender's Office (DPU) serves people there by appointment.

cic.name: CIC do Imigrante (São Paulo State Government)
cic.desc: Legal guidance, psychological and social support, courses and job referrals.

dpe.name: São Paulo State Public Defender's Office
dpe.desc: Free public lawyers for people who cannot pay. Help with housing, family, health and other rights.

dpu.name: Federal Public Defender's Office (DPU)
dpu.desc: Federal public defenders. Help with migration, asylum and Federal Police matters.

acnur.name: UNHCR Brazil (UN Refugee Agency)
acnur.desc: Information for refugees and asylum seekers, in several languages, on the Help website.

caritas.name: Cáritas Arquidiocesana de São Paulo
caritas.desc: Serves refugees and asylum seekers, in partnership with UNHCR.

meta.title: About the project | Welcome to Brazil
meta.desc: About the Welcome to Brazil guide: author, program, college, goal, sources and legal notice.

about.title: About the project
about.lead: Welcome to Brazil is a university outreach project.

goal.title: Goal
goal.text: To help migrants and refugees who have just arrived in Brazil by bringing together the essential information in one place: documents, work, transport, health, housing, education and where to get help.
goal.design: The website is light and was made for phones and limited internet, with large text and simple language.

method.title: Where the information comes from
method.text: The information was researched in official sources, such as gov.br, the Federal Police, Receita Federal, the Ministry of Labor and Employment, the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Justice, São Paulo City Hall, SPTrans, Metrô, CPTM and UNHCR. Each page shows its sources and the date they were checked.
method.verify: When we could not confirm information in an official source, it is marked “to be confirmed”.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.text: This website does not use cookies and does not collect personal data. Your chosen language is saved only on your device.

legal.1: This website is not an official service. It is not linked to any government agency or to the organizations listed.
legal.2: The information is for guidance only and does not replace services from official agencies or advice from a lawyer or public defender.
legal.3: Rules, prices, addresses and opening hours can change. Always check the official channels before going somewhere or paying a fee.
legal.title: Legal notice
